extraction.name: VQAonline
extraction.description: A fully authentic visual question answering dataset sourced from online question answering community forums, specifically Stack Exchange, where each example includes a natural language question, natural language context, image, and an accepted answer validated by the individual asking the question.
extraction.creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, Danna Gurari
extraction.citeAs: Chen, C., Liu, M., Codella, N., Li, Y., Yuan, L., and Gurari, D. Fully Authentic Visual Question Answering Dataset from Online Communities. arXiv:2311.15562v4, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by scraping publicly-available data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange. The authors collected examples containing a natural language question, natural language context, an image, and at least one answer, and only used examples where the person who posted the visual question marked an accepted answer. The original data on Stack Exchange was collected through user entry interactions: the question as the post title, the image as a URL link, the context in the body text field, and answers posted publicly by other users.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, User-generated content data, Passive Data Collection, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: After removing examples for which the image could not be downloaded from the provided link, the final dataset contained 64,696 visual questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Publicly-available Stack Exchange archive data in XML format hosted at https://archive.org/details/stackexchange, spanning 105 topical sites and containing user-posted questions, contexts, image links, answers, scores, and accepted-answer markings.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors filtered the scraped data in multiple stages. Starting from 330,705 candidate visual questions, they removed visual questions without an accepted answer, then removed visual questions with scores of 0 or less for either the question or answer, removed visual questions with multiple images, removed visual questions with visual answers, and removed examples for which the image could not be downloaded from the provided link. They also excluded 75 technology topics because they typically were language problems. For data format consistency, all images were converted to png format. Training and validation splits were created by randomly selecting 7 examples for training and 3 for validation from each topic with at least 20 examples; no topics were excluded from the test dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Examples were filtered to retain only those with four components: a natural language question, natural language context, image, and at least one answer, and only those with an accepted answer were used. Low-quality VQAs were removed using Stack Exchange scores, excluding examples with scores 0 or less for either the question or answer. Visual questions with multiple images or visual answers were excluded. Examples whose images could not be downloaded were removed. All images were converted to png format for consistency.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset includes authentic topic labels chosen by users through Stack Exchange topical communities. Additional annotations were created for analysis. For image content analysis, the authors manually labeled sampled images as screenshots or infographics. For image importance analysis, they manually labeled whether images were question-aligned, context-aligned, and necessary. For user intention, the authors developed an eight-category taxonomy through multi-round author analysis, then hired three Amazon Mechanical Turk crowdworkers to annotate the primary user intent for 105 randomly selected VQAs, one from each topic. Two independent workers labeled each item, and a third worker broke ties. For human evaluation of model outputs, ten domain experts each rated model-generated answers for 20 VQAs in their topic as incorrect (0), partially correct (0.5), or correct (1) using a home-grown web-based interface.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk; a home-grown web-based interface
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For user intention taxonomy development, two author-annotators conducted four rounds of annotation and discussion on 105 visual questions, resolving disagreements and refining definitions. Agreement accuracy improved from 53.3% to 87.5% and Cohen's kappa improved from 45.24% to 84.69%. For the crowdsourced user intention labels, two independent workers labeled each of 105 VQAs and a third worker broke ties for the 25 disagreements, yielding the final label by majority vote. For human evaluation of model answers, the authors compared quantitative metrics to human judgments using Pearson correlation and reported that LLaMA2, METEOR, and BERTscore aligned best with human judgments, while CLIP-S aligned least.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: User intention: 2 independent labels per item, with a 3rd label used to break ties when needed; human evaluation of model outputs: 1 domain expert rating per model-generated answer
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: For user intention annotation, three Amazon Mechanical Turk workers located in the United States, each with more than 500 completed HITs and over a 95% approval rating. For human evaluation, ten annotators who were domain experts in one of ten topics covered in the dataset, each with at least a Master's degree in a field related to their assigned VQA topic, and located in the United States.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper notes geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more users from countries like the US, India, and Europe and fewer from countries like Egypt.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors expect improved models designed for VQAonline to benefit real-world applications including other community question answering platforms, learning assistance VQA tools for children, virtual assistants, visual dialog and query, and visual search and browsing. They also note the dataset can facilitate further exploration of hallucination issues in authentic use cases.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and Internet. Geographic representation is unbalanced, with more from countries like US, India, and Europe and less from countries like Egypt. The dataset also excludes 75 technology topics because they typically are language problems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas and has unbalanced geographic representation. Topic distribution is highly imbalanced, with some topics having as few as 10 examples and others over 20,000. The authors also note that many benchmarked models may have seen Stack Exchange data during training, creating potential data contamination and unfair advantage in evaluation. Answers are atypically long, making standard VQA evaluation metrics ineffective for this dataset.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset supports few-shot learning and contains training, validation, and test splits of 665, 285, and 63,746 examples respectively. It is used in the paper for benchmarking zero-shot and one-shot VQA models, evaluating long-form answer generation, and studying evaluation metrics aligned with human judgment. The authors also position it as useful for improving VQA models for authentic community question answering and related real-world applications.
